title: Microwave Sparking & Arcing (Foil, Metal Rim, Twist Tie)
immediateAction: PRESS STOP IMMEDIATELY & UNPLUG FROM WALL. KEEP DOOR CLOSED IF FLAMES OCCUR.
description: Metal reflects high-frequency microwave radiation instead of absorbing it. Voltage gradients concentrate at thin metal edges, crinkled aluminum foil, or twist ties, ionizing surrounding air and creating a 2,000°F luminous plasma electrical arc that can puncture the cavity wall or ignite grease.

checklist.action: Cut electrical power immediately
checklist.detail: Press STOP or Cancel, then pull the electrical plug directly from the wall outlet to guarantee no residual microwave generation.

checklist.action: Do not open door if fire starts
checklist.detail: If sparks ignited paper towels, food containers, or grease, keep the door tightly shut. A closed microwave cavity is airtight and will extinguish the fire within 60-90 seconds by exhausting available oxygen.

checklist.action: Wait 3 minutes for plasma discharge to cool
checklist.detail: Allow the superheated metal and cavity surfaces to cool. Touching arced foil immediately can cause instant contact burns.

checklist.action: Remove the offending metal object using tongs or oven mitts
checklist.detail: Carefully remove the container or foil. Inspect the glass turntable and roller ring for heat cracking.

checklist.action: Inspect the interior mica waveguide cover
checklist.detail: Check the small rectangular mica paper cover on the right interior wall. If it shows black scorch marks, burn holes, or carbon tracking, it must be replaced before the microwave is ever turned on again.

whatNeverToDo: NEVER throw water into an electrical microwave oven (creates a catastrophic high-voltage electrocution hazard).
NEVER open the door while flames are actively flaring (the sudden burst of fresh oxygen creates a dangerous backdraft flare into your face).
NEVER restart the microwave without removing the metal and inspecting the mica waveguide cover (carbon residue sustains permanent arcing).
NEVER use metal twist ties, gold-rimmed ceramic mugs, or take-out boxes with wire handles in a microwave.

inspectionSteps: Inspect the enamel interior walls for bare metal exposure; exposed raw steel must be sealed with microwave cavity touch-up paint.
Check the mica waveguide cover on the right wall for carbon scorch holes.
Test cavity function safely by placing a microwave-safe mug of tap water inside and running on high for 45 seconds.
applianceHealth.replacementSigns: If the magnetron emits a deep loud buzzing rattle without heating, or if sparking continues inside the waveguide opening with no metal present, the magnetron tube is destroyed and the appliance must be replaced.

authorityStandard: UL 923 Standard for Microwave Cooking Appliances / FDA 21 CFR 1030.10 Performance Standards

title: Oven or Broiler Grease Fire
immediateAction: KEEP OVEN DOOR CLOSED! TURN OFF HEAT IMMEDIATELY. NEVER THROW WATER!
description: Fats and animal greases ignite spontaneously between 400°F and 450°F (204°C-232°C). Opening the oven door introduces an immediate surge of atmospheric oxygen, causing a sudden violent flashover fireball that can ignite kitchen cabinets, clothing, and hair.

checklist.action: Turn off the oven power or gas dial immediately
checklist.detail: Switch off temperature controls, broiler mode, or bake elements to stop adding thermal energy to the grease pool.

checklist.action: KEEP THE OVEN DOOR FIRMLY CLOSED
checklist.detail: A modern insulated oven cavity will starve grease flames of oxygen within 30 to 90 seconds if the door seal remains unbroken.

checklist.action: Turn on the range exhaust hood and open exterior windows
checklist.detail: Clear toxic carbon monoxide and acrid fat smoke from the kitchen, but do not open doors that cause direct high-velocity drafts toward the oven.

checklist.action: Monitor from 10 feet back with Class B/K fire extinguisher ready
checklist.detail: Keep an approved dry chemical or wet chemical fire extinguisher on hand. If flames breach door glass or smoke thickens after 2 minutes, initiate emergency home evacuation.

checklist.action: Allow oven to cool undisturbed for at least 60 minutes
checklist.detail: Do not open the door even after flames appear extinguished; trapped hot grease vapors can reignite instantaneously upon early air exposure.

whatNeverToDo: NEVER OPEN THE OVEN DOOR TO 'SEE HOW BIG THE FIRE IS' (introduces an oxygen blast that ignites a flashover into your face).
NEVER throw water or damp towels on a grease or oil fire (water violently flashes to steam, causing a 1,700x volume explosion of burning aerosolized oil droplets).
NEVER toss flour, cornstarch, or baking powder on a grease fire (flour is a combustible carbohydrate that creates a massive fireball explosion).
NEVER attempt to carry a flaming roasting pan or baking sheet out of the oven.

inspectionSteps: After cooling completely, inspect bake and broil heating elements for blistered sheath or severed electrical resistance wires.
Examine door glass and silicone/fiberglass perimeter gasket for thermal degradation or cracks.
Thoroughly clean all carbonized grease residues with baking soda degreaser before heating oven again.
applianceHealth.replacementSigns: If internal door glass shattered, wiring behind back panel melted, or digital control board displays permanent F-series thermal runaway errors, professional repair or unit replacement is mandatory.

authorityStandard: NFPA 96 Standard for Ventilation Control and Fire Protection / US Fire Administration Kitchen Safety

title: Stovetop Oil / Deep Fryer Pan Fire
immediateAction: SLIDE A FLAT METAL LID OVER THE PAN. TURN OFF BURNER. NEVER MOVE THE PAN.
description: Vegetable and frying oils reach auto-ignition temperature at 750°F-800°F (400°C-425°C). Burning oil spreads rapidly across kitchen surfaces if disturbed. Pouring even a teaspoon of water causes a volcanic liquid-expanding steam explosion that burns ceilings and skin.

checklist.action: Slide (do not drop) a metal lid or baking sheet over the pan
checklist.detail: Approach from the side shielding your hand and body behind the lid. Slide it smoothly across the pan rim to seal off all atmospheric oxygen.

checklist.action: Turn off the burner or heating dial immediately
checklist.detail: Cut the gas or electrical supply. If reaching the knob exposes your arms to flames, turn off the kitchen circuit breaker or master gas valve.

checklist.action: Leave the lid in place until completely cold (minimum 20 minutes)
checklist.detail: Removing the lid prematurely re-exposes superheated oil to fresh air, triggering instantaneous re-ignition.

checklist.action: Smother with copious pure baking soda or salt ONLY if lid is unavailable
checklist.detail: For early low-height pan flames, dump an entire box of pure sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) or table salt directly at the fire base to release smothering carbon dioxide.

checklist.action: If flames spread to range hood or cabinets: EVACUATE & DIAL 911 / 112
checklist.detail: Do not fight a grease fire that has escaped the pan. Evacuate all occupants and call emergency services immediately.

whatNeverToDo: NEVER POUR WATER ON BURNING OIL (produces an instant 10-foot fireball explosion).
NEVER pick up, slide, or carry the burning pan to the sink or outdoors (splashes boiling 700°F oil onto your chest, arms, and flooring).
NEVER use flour, cornstarch, or baking powder (they explode on contact with flames).
NEVER swat flames with a dish towel or apron (spreads oil and ignites your clothing).

inspectionSteps: Check range hood aluminum mesh grease filters for melted aluminum or ignited grease ducts.
Inspect glass-ceramic electric cooktop for heat fractures or burner coil delamination.
For gas stoves, ensure gas burner brass orifices are clear of carbonized oil.
applianceHealth.replacementSigns: If range hood wiring or exhaust fan housing melted, or cooktop tempered glass cracked, replace affected assemblies before cooking.

authorityStandard: NFPA 10 Standard for Portable Fire Extinguishers / FEMA Kitchen Fire Prevention

title: Thermal Shock Bakeware Shatter / Exploding Glass Dish
immediateAction: DO NOT TOUCH WITH BARE HANDS! STEP BACK IMMEDIATELY. EVACUATE PETS & CHILDREN.
description: Modern tempered soda-lime glass bakeware expands and contracts under temperature swings. Sudden uneven cooling (ΔT > 100°F / 55°C) creates extreme internal tensile stresses that overcome glass elasticity, detonating the dish into hundreds of high-velocity razor-sharp shards.

checklist.action: Freeze movement and warn everyone to stay back
checklist.detail: Ensure children, barefoot family members, and pets do not walk onto the kitchen floor. Glass slivers can travel over 10 feet across tile or hardwood.

checklist.action: Turn off heat and let glass cool completely for 45 minutes
checklist.detail: Hot shattered glass continues to fracture and pop as internal thermal gradients equalize. Do not attempt cleanup while fragments are sizzling.

checklist.action: Put on puncture-proof leather work gloves, eye protection, and closed shoes
checklist.detail: Never use thin rubber or latex dishwashing gloves, which hot jagged glass slices through effortlessly.

checklist.action: Condemn and discard all food within an 8-foot blast radius
checklist.detail: Exploding tempered glass sheds microscopic glass dust and sharp translucent needle splinters that penetrate deeply into food. Ingesting them causes severe gastrointestinal lacerations.

checklist.action: Clean up using cardboard, broom, vacuum, and damp paper towels
checklist.detail: Sweep large pieces into a rigid cardboard box (not a plastic bag that punctures). Vacuum thoroughly, then wipe the entire area with damp paper towels in a single direction to trap microscopic glass dust.

whatNeverToDo: NEVER salvage, rinse, or eat any food that was in or near the shattered glass dish.
NEVER place a hot glass casserole dish directly on a cold granite, marble, or stainless steel countertop, or in a wet sink.
NEVER add cold broth, tap water, or wine to a hot glass baking dish while in the oven.
NEVER use broil settings or stovetop burners on glass bakeware.

inspectionSteps: If explosion occurred inside the oven, inspect the bottom heating element casing and convection fan blades for wedged glass.
Vacuum the oven floor, door seal channels, and bottom drawer with a shop vac.
Verify oven door fiberglass gasket has no glass shards trapped in the woven weave.
applianceHealth.replacementSigns: If flying shards pitted or cracked the inner oven door glass pane, replace the door glass assembly before running the oven at high temperatures.

authorityStandard: ASTM C149 Standard Test Method for Thermal Shock Resistance of Glass Containers

title: Dishwasher Suds Volcano (Liquid Dish Soap in Dishwasher)
immediateAction: CANCEL CYCLE IMMEDIATELY! DO NOT RUN RINSE CYCLE. DUMP VEGETABLE OIL OR SALT.
description: Standard liquid hand dish soap contains high-foaming sodium laureth sulfate surfactants designed for sink washing. The high-pressure 140°F spray jets in a dishwasher agitate this into dense shaving-cream suds that breach the door seal, flood flooring, and cause pump motor cavitation.

checklist.action: Cancel cycle and cut power immediately
checklist.detail: Press CANCEL or DRAIN. If the keypad is unresponsive, switch off the dishwasher's wall switch or circuit breaker.

checklist.action: Dam the floor with towels and blankets
checklist.detail: Surround the dishwasher base kickplate with dry towels to prevent suds and soapy water from seeping into subflooring or baseboards.

checklist.action: Open door and scoop out maximum foam volume
checklist.detail: Use a wide plastic dustpan, shallow bowl, or towels to scoop as much foam as possible out of the tub and racks into a bucket.

checklist.action: Pour 1/2 cup cooking oil (or 1/2 cup table salt) directly on tub floor
checklist.detail: Vegetable, canola, or olive oil acts as an immediate industrial defoaming agent by dramatically altering surface tension, instantly collapsing soap bubbles into liquid.

checklist.action: Run a Drain cycle, followed by a distilled white vinegar rinse
checklist.detail: Run a 2-minute Drain cycle. Pour 2 cups of white vinegar onto the bottom to break residual soap film, then run a short normal cycle without detergent.

whatNeverToDo: NEVER run a standard 'Rinse' cycle hoping water will wash away the suds (hot pressurized water multiplies bubbles tenfold, flooding the motor pump).
NEVER put hand dish soap (Dawn, Fairy, Palmolive) or body wash into a dishwasher under any circumstances.
NEVER leave soapy flood water sitting under the dishwasher overnight (corrodes wiring, triggers anti-flood sensor lockouts like Bosch E15, and breeds subfloor mold).
NEVER use electric shop vacuums on water unless explicitly rated as wet/dry vacuums.

inspectionSteps: Check beneath the lower front kickplate with a flashlight to verify no water has pooled in the base overflow tray.
If the dishwasher displays an error code (e.g., E15, i30) and continuously runs the drain pump with the door open, the flood float switch has tripped.
Allow base pan to dry completely (use a fan) for 24 hours to reset float switch before reuse.
applianceHealth.replacementSigns: If circulation wash pump makes a loud grinding squeal or water leaks through the motor shaft seal during subsequent washes, pump seals must be replaced.

authorityStandard: AHAM DW-1 Household Dishwashers Safety and Performance Standards

dangerBadge: TOXIC PYROLYSIS GAS & PET BIRD MORTALITY
title: Overheated / Burnt Teflon Fumes (Polymer Fume Fever & Avian Toxicity)
immediateAction: EVACUATE PET BIRDS TO FRESH AIR IMMEDIATELY! TURN ON EXHAUST HOOD. CROSS-VENTILATE.
description: PTFE (Teflon) begins thermal degradation at 500°F (260°C) and undergoes rapid pyrolysis above 660°F (350°C), releasing submicron fluorinated polymer particles and toxic gases including perfluoroisobutylene (PFIB), carbonyl fluoride, and hydrogen fluoride. Birds die within minutes due to acute hemorrhagic pulmonary edema.

checklist.action: Turn off heat burner immediately
checklist.detail: Shut off the stove burner immediately. Do not lift or shake the pan.

checklist.action: EVACUATE ALL PET BIRDS OUTDOORS OR TO A VENTILATED SEPARATE FLOOR
checklist.detail: Avian respiratory anatomy (air sacs and high-efficiency gas exchange) makes birds hypersensitive to PTFE pyrolysis. Move birds immediately to fresh outdoor air.

checklist.action: Engage maximum kitchen exhaust ventilation
checklist.detail: Switch range hood fan to highest speed and open all kitchen exterior doors and windows to generate strong cross-ventilation.

checklist.action: Evacuate humans and pets from the kitchen area for 45 minutes
checklist.detail: Remain out of the kitchen until smoke, haze, and pungent acrid odor have completely dissipated.

checklist.action: Monitor for Polymer Fume Fever ('Teflon Flu') symptoms
checklist.detail: Symptoms appear 4-8 hours post-exposure: severe chills, fever (101°F-104°F), chest tightness, dry cough, headache, and muscle aches. Seek emergency medical care if breathing becomes labored.

whatNeverToDo: NEVER plunge the overheated smoking pan into a cold sink of water (causes an explosive steam cloud carrying concentrated toxic PFIB and fluoropolymers straight into your respiratory tract).
NEVER preheat an empty non-stick skillet on high heat (empty pans hit 500°F in under 2 minutes).
NEVER attempt to recondition or continue cooking with a pan whose coating turned brown, blistered, or off-gassed (it permanently sheds toxic particles).
NEVER keep pet birds in or near kitchens where non-stick cookware is used.

inspectionSteps: Let the overheated pan cool naturally to room temperature on the cold stove or outdoors.
Inspect the coating under bright light: browning, peeling, bubbling, or chalky white residue confirms irreversible polymer breakdown.
Bag the cookware securely and discard permanently in household trash.
applianceHealth.replacementSigns: Non-stick cookware that has undergone pyrolysis cannot be repaired, re-seasoned, or restored. Discard immediately and replace with cast iron, carbon steel, or 18/10 stainless steel.

authorityStandard: CDC / NIOSH Health Hazard Guidelines for Fluorocarbon Polymers / Journal of Avian Medicine

title: Exploding Sealed Food or Whole Egg in Microwave
immediateAction: DO NOT OPEN DOOR FOR AT LEAST 5 MINUTES! SUPERHEATED POCKETS EXPLODE ON CONTACT.
description: Microwaves rapidly vibrate water molecules inside food, generating high internal steam pressures. In intact whole eggs, sealed plastic containers, or unbroken egg yolks, the outer membrane acts as a pressure vessel. When pierced or agitated upon door opening, instant flash-boiling triggers a delayed explosion.

checklist.action: Stop microwave cycle and leave door completely closed
checklist.detail: Press STOP or unplug the appliance. Do not open the door even if you hear a pop or the cycle finishes.

checklist.action: Wait a mandatory 5-minute cooldown period
checklist.detail: Superheated pockets of liquid water (above 212°F / 100°C) remain unstable. Disturbing them prematurely triggers explosive vaporization.

checklist.action: Wear glasses or face shield before opening the door
checklist.detail: Shield your face and eyes. Stand to the hinge side and open the door slowly at arm's length.

checklist.action: Do not pierce or cut warm eggs or sealed dishes with a fork
checklist.detail: Delayed explosions frequently occur outside the microwave when a fork punctures an intact yolk or sealed plastic film.

checklist.action: Inspect microwave door latch and radiation seal
checklist.detail: Violent internal pressure detonations can warp the microwave door frame or crack the tempered viewing glass, compromising microwave containment.

whatNeverToDo: NEVER rush to open the door immediately after hearing an internal food pop or bang.
NEVER microwave whole eggs in shells, raw whole eggs with unbroken yolks, sealed baby food jars, or unvented mason jars.
NEVER lean your face directly over microwaved food when piercing with a utensil.
NEVER use the microwave if the door latch is cracked or does not seal completely flush.

inspectionSteps: Wipe away all food splatter from interior cavity, especially the waveguide cover and ceiling stirrer fan.
Check that the door interlock safety switches click firmly and door has zero play when latched.
Inspect the black mesh screen in the door window for cracks or separation.
applianceHealth.replacementSigns: If the door does not close airtight, or if the outer or inner glass pane has fractured from pressure shock, the microwave must be discarded to prevent radiation leakage.

authorityStandard: FDA Center for Devices and Radiological Health / Acoustical Society of America Egg Cavitation Study

title: Refrigerator Chemical Hiss / Refrigerant (R600a/Freon) Leak
immediateAction: UNPLUG REFRIGERATOR. DO NOT FLIP LIGHT SWITCHES (IGNITION HAZARD). VENTILATE.
description: Modern household refrigerators use R600a (isobutane), which is an odorless or faintly sweet, highly flammable hydrocarbon gas. Older units use hydrofluorocarbons (R134a) or ammonia in RV refrigerators. Puncturing coils releases pressurized gas that can ignite from light switch sparks or cause asphyxiation.

checklist.action: Unplug the refrigerator from the wall outlet
checklist.detail: Kill power at the plug or circuit breaker to stop the compressor from running dry and overheating.

checklist.action: DO NOT touch light switches, lighters, or electrical appliances
checklist.detail: If your refrigerator uses R600a isobutane, electrical arcing inside a standard wall switch or outlet can ignite the flammable gas cloud.

checklist.action: Open exterior windows and exterior doors for cross-ventilation
checklist.detail: Allow dense refrigerant gas (heavier than air) to dissipate from low kitchen floor pockets to the outdoors.

checklist.action: Evacuate the kitchen until chemical smell or hissing ceases
checklist.detail: Refrigerant vapors displace breathable oxygen and can trigger cardiac arrhythmia, dizziness, and respiratory distress if inhaled.

checklist.action: Call a certified EPA Section 608 refrigeration technician
checklist.detail: Do not attempt to seal punctured aluminum evaporator lines with epoxy, duct tape, or solder. Professional brazing and vacuum recovery is legally required.

whatNeverToDo: NEVER use metal knives, ice picks, chisels, or screwdrivers to scrape frost or ice from freezer walls (the #1 cause of punctured refrigerant coils).
NEVER strike matches, smoke cigarettes, or operate stoves while refrigerant is leaking.
NEVER consume uncovered food or ice cubes that have been exposed to chemical refrigerant mist or compressor oil.
NEVER leave a punctured running refrigerator plugged in (moisture gets sucked into the sealed compressor, destroying it permanently).

inspectionSteps: A punctured sealed refrigeration system cannot cool and will permanently fail without professional repair.
Discard all open food, produce, and ice cubes exposed to refrigerant mist.
Schedule an EPA-certified repair service to assess if line brazing and recharge is economically viable.
applianceHealth.replacementSigns: If evaporator puncture is extensive or compressor ingested moisture and burned out, purchasing a replacement refrigerator is generally more cost-effective than sealed system rebuilding.

authorityStandard: EPA Section 608 Clean Air Act / UL 60335-2-24 Flammable Refrigerant Standards

title: Melted Plastic on Oven Element or Dishwasher Heating Coil
immediateAction: TURN OFF APPLIANCE IMMEDIATELY. VENTILATE TO AVOID TOXIC FUMES. LET COOL COMPLETELY.
description: Thermoplastics (polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, PVC) melt between 250°F and 350°F and decompose rapidly on 800°F exposed electric heating elements. The resulting acrid smoke releases toxic volatile organic compounds (VOCs), phthalates, styrene, and toxic carbonaceous residue.

checklist.action: Turn off the oven or dishwasher power immediately
checklist.detail: Stop heating immediately to prevent plastic from reaching combustion point or dripping through floor grates.

checklist.action: Evacuate children and ventilate the kitchen aggressively
checklist.detail: Turn exhaust fan on high and open windows. Do not inhale the dense gray-white smoke, which irritates mucous membranes and triggers asthma.

checklist.action: Do NOT attempt to wipe or scrape hot molten plastic
checklist.detail: Molten plastic adheres aggressively to human skin like liquid napalm, causing immediate third-degree contact burns.

checklist.action: Chill the plastic with an ice bag once safe to handle
checklist.detail: After the heating element is warm (not red hot), place a bag filled with ice cubes directly against the plastic puddle. Chilling makes plastic brittle and shrinks it slightly away from metal.

checklist.action: Pop the cold brittle plastic off using a wooden or stiff plastic scraper
checklist.detail: Pry gently between the cold metal coil and plastic mass. It will chip off in large solid chunks without damaging the metal sheath.

whatNeverToDo: NEVER run the oven 'Self-Clean' cycle to burn off melted plastic (creates a lethal concentration of toxic fumes and can trigger an uncontrollable grease/plastic oven fire).
NEVER use metal razor blades, screwdrivers, or wire brushes directly on tubular heating elements (scratches puncture the outer alloy sheath, causing an electrical short circuit).
NEVER cook food in an oven or run dishes in a dishwasher until every trace of burnt plastic odor is eradicated.

inspectionSteps: After mechanical removal, rub stubborn spots with a paste of baking soda and a non-abrasive nylon scrubber.
Wipe element clean with a damp microfiber cloth and allow to dry.
Test element by heating oven to 250°F with windows open for 15 minutes to confirm zero residual off-gassing.
applianceHealth.replacementSigns: If the heating element sheath has pitted, blistered, or displays a visible hole with white internal magnesium oxide insulation showing, replace the heating element before using the oven.

authorityStandard: OSHA Toxic and Hazardous Substances 29 CFR 1910.1000 / Consumer Product Safety Commission

title: Dishwasher Acrid Electrical Burning Smell or Smoke
immediateAction: KILL CIRCUIT BREAKER IMMEDIATELY! DO NOT TOUCH APPLIANCE IN STANDING WATER.
description: High current loads (10-15 amps) combined with moisture exposure make dishwasher wiring harnesses, control boards, and circulation pump motors vulnerable to resistive heating, melted wire nuts, and electrical smoldering fires beneath the tub.

checklist.action: Trip the circuit breaker in your electrical service panel
checklist.detail: Locate your breaker box and immediately switch the dishwasher's dedicated breaker to OFF. Do not attempt to unplug if the outlet is behind the unit or wet.

checklist.action: DO NOT stand in pooled water while touching the dishwasher
checklist.detail: Standing water combined with an ungrounded or shorted electrical harness creates a lethal electrocution path.

checklist.action: Keep the dishwasher door firmly latched
checklist.detail: Keeping the door closed prevents room air from fueling smoldering wires inside the door control console.

checklist.action: Have a Class C (electrical) fire extinguisher on standby
checklist.detail: Never use water on an electrical appliance fire. If flames emerge from beneath the kickplate, discharge a dry chemical extinguisher.

checklist.action: Schedule an appliance repair specialist or licensed electrician
checklist.detail: Do not re-energize the circuit breaker until a technician has removed the door panel and inspected terminal blocks, run capacitors, and pump motor windings.

whatNeverToDo: NEVER pour water over an electrical appliance that smells like burning wires (causes catastrophic electric shock and arc blast).
NEVER reset the circuit breaker if it tripped on an electrical burning smell without an internal inspection.
NEVER touch metal trim or door handle with bare feet on wet flooring.

inspectionSteps: Leave power completely disconnected.
Remove lower access kickplate and inspect wiring junction box for melted wire nuts or scorched Romex cable.
Remove outer door panel to inspect main control printed circuit board (PCB) for burnt solder joints or swollen capacitors.
applianceHealth.replacementSigns: If the main wiring harness is melted or the plastic inner control console is charred, harness replacement often exceeds the residual value of the machine; replace the unit.

authorityStandard: NFPA 70 National Electrical Code / CPSC Dishwasher Recall Safety Guidelines

title: Air Fryer Parchment Paper Caught in Heating Element
immediateAction: UNPLUG AIR FRYER IMMEDIATELY! DO NOT PULL BASKET OUT (PREVENTS FLAME BLOWOUT).
description: Air fryers utilize high-velocity convection blowers circulating air at rapid speeds. Placing loose or lightweight parchment paper or wax paper into the basket without sufficient food weight causes the air vortex to suck the paper straight up into the 400°F exposed red-hot heating coil, instantly igniting paper flames.

checklist.action: Yank the electrical plug from the wall outlet immediately
checklist.detail: Cutting power instantly shuts down the convection fan, reducing the oxygen draft feeding the ignited paper.

checklist.action: KEEP THE AIR FRYER DRAWER CLOSED
checklist.detail: Do not yank open the drawer! Pulling the basket out supplies sudden oxygen that blows active flames into your face and onto countertops.

checklist.action: Wait 90 seconds for fire to suffocate inside the metal cavity
checklist.detail: A small paper fire will consume available interior oxygen and burn out rapidly within the enclosed metal basket.

checklist.action: If smoke continues or escapes: smother with a wet towel or discharge fire extinguisher
checklist.detail: Drape a damp (not dripping) towel tightly over the top and rear air exhaust vents to choke remaining oxygen.

checklist.action: Once cold, remove all charred paper residue from the heating coil
checklist.detail: Wear gloves and use a damp cloth to clean carbonized paper remnants wrapped around the spiral heating element before ever powering on again.

whatNeverToDo: NEVER preheat an air fryer with loose parchment paper inside (without heavy food pinning it down, it WILL fly into the coil and ignite).
NEVER use wax paper in an air fryer (wax melts at 135°F, producing combustible hydrocarbon wax vapors).
NEVER pull out the burning drawer onto laminate, quartz, or wood countertops.
NEVER leave an operating air fryer unattended near flammable paper towels or beneath wooden cabinets.

inspectionSteps: Invert appliance (when completely cold and unplugged) to inspect heating element spiral for remaining charred paper.
Check that fan blades rotate freely without friction against bent coils.
Test run outdoors or under maximum range hood ventilation for 3 minutes without food to ensure zero smoke.
applianceHealth.replacementSigns: If the upper plastic casing or fan blade assembly deformed from heat, or internal thermal fuse tripped permanently, replace the air fryer.

authorityStandard: UL 1026 Standard for Electric Household Cooking and Food Serving Appliances

title: Exploding Glass Bottle or Carbonated Can in Freezer
immediateAction: DO NOT OPEN FREEZER ABRUPTLY. WEAR THICK GLOVES BEFORE TOUCHING.
description: Water expands by approximately 9% in volume upon freezing, generating hydraulic pressures exceeding 25,000 to 40,000 psi against rigid containers. When sealed glass beer/wine bottles or carbonated beverage cans freeze solid, the extreme pressure fractures glass into razor-sharp projectiles and splits aluminum cans.

checklist.action: Put on thick work gloves and safety glasses
checklist.detail: Sub-zero chilled glass shards are brittle and razor-sharp. Frostbite from handling frozen metal cans combined with glass cuts poses high injury risk.

checklist.action: Lay a heavy bath towel over the freezer shelf before moving
checklist.detail: Prevent glass slivers from falling down internal evaporator air ducts, defrost drains, or wire basket tracks.

checklist.action: Discard any open, perforated, or paper-wrapped frozen food packages
checklist.detail: High-velocity glass shards and carbonated spray contaminate frozen foods with invisible micro-shards.

checklist.action: Carefully remove broken bottle remnants into a sturdy cardboard box
checklist.detail: Never place jagged heavy glass fragments into thin plastic garbage bags that tear instantly.

checklist.action: Wipe down interior walls and floor with damp microfiber cloths
checklist.detail: Wipe thoroughly in one direction to collect microscopic glass slivers, and clear frozen soda sludge before it glazes onto shelves.

whatNeverToDo: NEVER pour hot or warm water over frozen shattered glass to melt the ice (causes violent secondary thermal shock explosions).
NEVER freeze sealed glass beer, wine, or sparkling cider bottles to 'quick-chill' them without setting a 15-minute phone timer.
NEVER consume ice cubes from the freezer icemaker until the entire compartment is cleaned and cycled.

inspectionSteps: Check bottom defrost drain hole with a flashlight to ensure no glass shards are wedged inside, which causes future ice sheet flooding.
Inspect plastic door shelves and wire racks for stress cracks.
Ensure freezer door magnetic gasket seals airtight with no wedged glass fragments.
applianceHealth.replacementSigns: If expanding ice or glass impact punctured the inner plastic liner into the polyurethane foam insulation, seal the puncture with food-grade silicone sealant.

authorityStandard: ISO 7459 Glass Containers Thermal Shock Resistance / Glass Packaging Institute Safety Rules
